claim: Proximal Origin argued against laboratory-based scenarios.
limitations: The authors' conclusion is not a laboratory audit.

claim: The 2021 joint report ranked a laboratory incident extremely unlikely.
limitations: Joint-team finding; distinguish subsequent WHO leadership position.

claim: Tedros challenged the adequacy of the assessment on publication day.
limitations: It is inaccurate to claim WHO never reconsidered.

claim: The original confidence exceeded what the limited investigation justified.
limitations: A judgment about confidence, not proof of origin.

claim: WHO's reviewed current assessment favours zoonosis but leaves origin unresolved.
limitations: Not a claim of equal probabilities or a settled laboratory origin.

claim: WHO criticised delayed Chinese CDC market-data disclosure.
limitations: Affects investigation of animal origins too.

claim: NIH and EcoHealth had oversight and reporting deficiencies.
limitations: Audit did not independently adjudicate experimental science or causation; EcoHealth disputed key findings.

claim: HHS imposed a ten-year WIV debarment over a possible grant-terms violation, aggravated by records failures.
limitations: Uncontested administrative determination; not a criminal or causal judgment.

claim: HHS issued five-year EcoHealth and Daszak debarment notices in January 2025.
limitations: Periods include preceding suspensions; no appeal or modification found in a bounded search on 2026-11-17, but SAM.gov records were not checked.

claim: The Lancet expanded Daszak's competing-interest disclosure in June 2021.
limitations: Does not establish all scientific claims were false.

claim: Proximal Origin Slack messages from February to April 2020 were public by July 2023.
limitations: Not necessarily the first disclosure date for each message.

claim: Apart from two messages on 30 April 2020, none of the 11,305 messages in the July 2026 Senate release were found in the two July 2023 collections.
limitations: Compared by text matching with OCR for the 2023 screenshots; short messages not compared individually; other 2023-2026 publications not checked.

claim: The lab-leak Wikipedia article already covers WHO reassessment.
limitations: Retrieved page may be cached; pinned fetch failed.

claim: The reviewed origins article's WHO Phase 2 subsection ends at the 2022 report.
limitations: Other parts of the article contain newer information.

claim: Wikipedia should make current assessment and missing-data limitations clearer.
limitations: Editorial recommendation, not evidence of intentional suppression.

claim: WHO should explicitly acknowledge overconfidence and explain reforms.
limitations: WHO has not made this acknowledgment or these commitments; the proposal describes what an adequate acknowledgment would contain, not wording for WHO.

claim: Governments and scientists called for transparent investigation in 2021.
limitations: Calls for research do not establish origin.

claim: House minority staff raised possible EcoHealth misrepresentation concerns.
limitations: Political report, not final adjudication.

claim: OIG's tracker records 15 of 16 NIH/EcoHealth audit recommendations as closed implemented and one as open.
limitations: Closure reflects OIG acceptance of agency-reported action; supporting evidence is not published.

claim: OIG records as unimplemented the recommendation that NIH define 'immediate notification', which NIH committed in January 2023 to address within 90 days.
limitations: Tracker last update received 21 October 2024; expected April 2025 update not recorded. Bounded Guide-notice search only.

claim: SAGO recorded that 508 early-patient sequences requested from the China National Center for Bioinformation had not been released.
limitations: As of the June 2025 report; later provision not found in a bounded search.

claim: SAGO recorded that WHO's request for audits, documentation and staff interviews at WIV and the Wuhan CDC laboratory was refused.
limitations: SAGO's account; China disputes that requests were justified.

claim: WHO said it had requested, but not received, underlying data and non-public intelligence reports from governments including the US and Germany.
limitations: US status from a wire report of a February 2026 press conference; Germany said it would revert.

claim: China's National Health Commission said China shared origins data 'without reservation' and rejected some SAGO requests as groundless.
limitations: Reported by state media; a statement of position, not evidence of what was shared.

claim: We did not find a Nature Medicine editorial note or formal published response to criticisms of Proximal Origin.
limitations: Bounded search; a July 2023 press remark is known only secondhand; private correspondence not reviewed.

claim: The Lancet's editor told MPs disclosures are taken on trust and that Daszak's June 2021 disclosure should have been in the original letter.
limitations: Oral testimony; no published policy change describing revised disclosure review was found.

claim: In February 2020, 27 scientists published a statement in The Lancet condemning 'conspiracy theories suggesting that COVID-19 does not have a natural origin'.
limitations: Documents the statement, not whether its scientific claims were justified.

claim: Facebook removed posts claiming COVID-19 was man-made or manufactured from February 2021 and stopped doing so on 26 May 2021.
limitations: The policy concerned manufacture claims, not an accidental escape of a natural virus.

claim: The COVID-19 misinformation article presents the lack of evidence for a laboratory origin without stating that requested laboratory records were withheld, and does not cover how the misinformation label was applied to the lab-leak hypothesis.
limitations: Observation of one revision; volunteer-maintained article; bounded search.
